display.title: Episode 117: The Sly Fox and the Cheese (Purim)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's pre-Purim show: hearing every word of the Megillah, Shema with a young guest, and the fable of the fox in the well, which teaches how tricky the yetzer hara is.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week before Purim 5744, which fell on a Sunday. Uncle Yossi reminds children to make noise only at Haman's name, to hear every word of the Megillah, and to walk into shul proudly, since the Purim miracle came in the merit of the children Mordechai taught. After the Hakochainik march and the sponsor, story time begins with a hungry fox who mistakes the moon's reflection for cheese and lowers himself to the bottom of a well. A seven-year-old guest recites the Shema. Uncle Yossi then explains why the Torah was given to people and not to angels: we have a yetzer hara, a sly enemy who disguises himself. The fox escapes by tricking a second fox into the well, and Uncle Yossi draws the lesson: be alert, don't argue with the yetzer hara, and fight him with Torah, prayer and tzedakah. The show ends with the Tzivos Hashem Purim missions and Purim wishes.
display.lesson: The yetzer hara is sly and tricky: stay alert, don't argue with him, and weaken him with Torah, davening and tzedakah.

date.note: 'This coming Sunday is Purim', Megillah on Shabbos night (Purim 5744 = Sunday 18 March); one week after episode 116 (2 Adar II).
